claims.location: source name, characteristics[organism], characteristics[organism part], characteristics[material type], characteristics[individual] rows 1-5
claims.value: four archaeological human femoral cortical-bone samples plus a digestion blank
claims.evidence: The PRIDE protocol specifies human femoral cortical bone, four individual codes ar, ay, n, oo, and a digestion blank. Each exact RAW filename contains the matching AT code. The paper identifies the cemetery cohort and bone material.

claims.location: characteristics[osteocalcin concentration group], factor value[osteocalcin concentration group] rows 1-5
claims.value: ar and n high; ay and oo low; blank not applicable
claims.evidence: The PRIDE sample protocol explicitly identifies ar and n as the highest osteocalcin samples and ay and oo as the lowest.

claims.value: all five deposited RAW runs once each
claims.evidence: PRIDE lists five RAW files, each bearing an AT code that matches the protocol's four sample codes or the stated blank.

claims.location: comment[instrument], comment[proteomics data acquisition method], comment[cleavage agent details], comment[collision energy], comment[ms2 mass analyzer] rows 1-5
claims.value: Q Exactive HF-X, Top12 DDA, overnight trypsin digestion, normalized collision energy 28, Orbitrap MS2
claims.evidence: The PRIDE protocol states the instrument, Top12 method, trypsin digestion, normalized collision energy, and MS2 resolution. HCD and Orbitrap MS2 analyzer are inferred from the HF-X instrument and protocol details.

claims.location: comment[modification parameters], comment[fragment mass tolerance] rows 1-5
claims.value: six stated variable search modifications; fragment tolerance not available
claims.evidence: PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol explicitly lists oxidation M, deamidation N/Q, Gln->pyro-Glu, Glu->pyro-Glu, carbamidomethylation C, and gamma carboxylation E as variable modifications. It does not state a fragment mass tolerance.

limitations: Age, sex, and pathology are not mapped to the four run codes; those cells remain not available.
The ATbk code is interpreted as the stated digestion blank; the deposit does not explicitly expand that code.
HCD and Orbitrap MS2 analyzer are instrument-based inferences, not literal protocol labels.
The wet-lab enzyme is trypsin; MaxQuant's semi-specific Trypsin/P search setting is not used as the cleavage-agent value.
The full instrument RAW headers were not read.

The deposited MaxQuant output archive could not be independently inspected in this review environment, so the SDRF uses only the six modifications stated in PRIDE and leaves fragment tolerance not available.
